Noah (People Ops): Quick drop: condensed OKR + self-review guidance for the upcoming cycle. One-pager + copy button: https://redwoodinference.docs/hr/okrs-short-2026
Zoe (Eng Manager): Can we get a 3-line manager checklist I can paste into team sprint notes?
Noah (People Ops): Sure — paste this:
1) Confirm team has 3 priority OKRs, each with an owner and a measurable signal;
2) Each direct submits a 1-page self-review + 1 dev growth goal;
3) Manager adds a 1-2 paragraph note + rating and records calibration 1:1 date.
people-ops-bot: Reminder scheduled — self-reviews open 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC.
Hiro (IC): Micro self-review starter would be 🔥. I always get stuck with wording.
Noah (People Ops): Tiny starter you can copy:
"What I shipped (2-4 bullets)
Impact (quantified if possible; links to dashboards/demos)
Key blockers & learnings
Goals for next quarter (include 1 dev skill)
What I need from my manager (specific)"
Zoe (Eng Manager): Any examples for behavioral / leadership goals for senior ICs?
Noah (People Ops): Example behavioral goals:
- "Improve cross-team communication: run one cross-functional sync per sprint and reduce handoff questions by X%."
- "Mentorship: hold 1 office hour / week and document 3 coaching outcomes per quarter."
- "Decision quality: draft team postmortems for three incidents and lead retro action followups."
Maya (Recruiting): Quick Q — if someone joins mid-quarter, do we expect a full set of OKRs?
Noah (People Ops): No. For hires <6 weeks in the cycle, add a ramp-oriented goal (onboarding + one contribution). Managers mark them as "Ramp" and note a 90-day plan in the manager note.
Hiro (IC): How strict are Committed vs Stretch labels? People might pad committed.
Noah (People Ops): Committed = what you plan to deliver this quarter. Stretch = upside. Managers should call out padding during calibration and adjust expectations in the manager note.
Zoe (Eng Manager): We need a short rating rubric to align managers — can you paste something concise?
Noah (People Ops): Rating rubric (copyable):
- Exceeds: Clear, measurable impact beyond expectations; independent delivery and influence.
- Meets: Delivered expected outcomes with solid execution and collaboration.
- Needs Improvement: Missed key outcomes or inconsistent execution; manager plan required.
Also include 1 example sentence for each level in the doc.
people-ops-bot: Calendar event created — "OKR calibration sync" 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC (company).
Zoe (Eng Manager): If a long-running infra project slips a milestone, how should that be reflected?
Noah (People Ops): Document the updated timeline, blockers, and mitigation plan in both the IC's self-review and the manager note. Don't mark Needs Improvement solely for documented, reasonable slippage.
Maya (Recruiting): Anything managers should flag to people ops during calibration?
Noah (People Ops): Flag cases where ratings differ across managers for the same level, promo candidates, or accommodation/leave considerations that affected delivery. DM us if you need an alternate deadline.
Hiro (IC): Final Q: can we get a one-click team copy so we all use same format?
Noah (People Ops): Yes — the one-click team copy is live in the doc (link above). Use it to seed your template and then customize metrics.
Zoe (Eng Manager): Thanks — I'll run a 15-min examples slot in my next team sync and push the one-pager.
Noah (People Ops): Deadlines: self-reviews due 2026-04-10 09:00 UTC; manager reviews due 2026-04-17 17:00 UTC. Ping if you need alternate timelines. :sparkles:
